subject: Synapse Health — post-call compatibility summary & integration action plan
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Kira Thompson <kira@synapsehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Synapse Health — post-call compatibility summary & integration action plan

Hi Kira / Aidan —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to make next steps explicit. I’ve summarized what we heard, product fit items, and immediate asks.

What we heard (pain & goal summary)
- Primary pain: inconsistent clinical-content ranking and long inference tail when clinicians interact with long patient histories (latency spikes at ~3k tokens).
- Business goal: reduce time-to-answer for triage workflows from ~14s to <5s median while keeping quality parity for top-3 ranked results.
- Operational constraints: must run within Synapse’s Azure environment, SSO/SAML + SCIM for users, strict audit retention (13 months), and a PII-handling policy that disallows sending PHI outside of a VPC for production data.

Product / integration fit (what we proposed)
- Host a pilot on Redwood Dedicated in Azure region to meet data isolation and latency SLOs.
- SDK changes: lightweight streaming client + KV-preserving session tokens to support long conversation context without re-sending patient history each request. See attached redwood_sdk_change_notes_v0.3.pdf for proposed API surface and migration notes.
- Function calling & structured outputs: recommend function-calling for discrete structured extraction (diagnosis codes, triage priority) with JSON schema enforcement to simplify downstream ingestion.
- Embeddings & reranking: hybrid flow — embed candidate notes with Synapse’s on-prem retriever, send top-K for rerank to Redwood; propose using 1024-d float16 quantized embeddings for cost/latency trade-offs.

Risks / technical unknowns
- Exact peak concurrency during morning triage window (you mentioned 120 concurrent clinicians; confirm).
- Acceptable P99 latency for critical triage (is 10s acceptable?)
- Data residency — confirm whether Synapse requires offline/on-prem only for PHI or if dedicated VNet peering is sufficient for pilot.

Immediate next actions (owner / ETA)
1) Redwood: share SDK change notes and a short implementation checklist (attached). Owner: me. ETA: 48 hours.
2) Synapse: confirm concurrency and P99 SLO target; provide contact for SSO/SAML integration. Owner: Kira / Aidan. ETA: 2 business days.
3) Redwood infra: propose a pilot deployment topology (dedicated pool + VNet peering + audit log config). Owner: Ben Carter. ETA: 3 business days.
4) Joint: schedule a tech deep-dive to validate function-calling mapping and rerank pipeline. Proposed times: Thu 7/30 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 7/31 9:00–10:00 PT.

Attachments included: redwood_sdk_change_notes_v0.3.pdf, mutual-action-plan-synapse.xlsx

If that looks right, please reply with priority confirmations and preferred slot for the deep-dive. I’ll send a calendar invite after we lock it.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jul 28, 2026 at 11:02 AM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to make next steps explicit. ...

Adding a couple of technical clarifications that will feed the infra/design doc I’ll put together:
- Latency expectations: if target is median <5s and P99 <10s we should size for peak concurrency *and* consider continuous batching with per-tenant low-latency lanes (we can do 1–2ms extra tail to get 10–20% throughput improvement).
- Long context: we’ll use KV-cache preservation + streaming chunking at the SDK layer to avoid resending entire histories. That requires adding a session token (stateless pointer) and a small change to the SDK: session.start(), session.append_kv(), session.commit(). See attached note.
- Embedding quantization: 8-bit dynamic quantization works for rerank candidates; if Synapse needs higher fidelity we can fallback to float16 for top-10 candidates. Latency trade: float16 adds ~10–15% token latency depending on GPU selection.
- Function-calling mapping: for triage I suggest two function signatures — extract_triage_struct and classify_priority. We should lock the JSON schema in the deep-dive.

I’ll draft the deployment topology (dedicated GPU pool + autoscale triggers for morning triage) and an audit-log configuration that meets 13-month retention.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Synapse Health — post-call compatibility summary & integration action plan

Monica / Ben —

Appreciate the clear summary. Confirming the core priorities from our side:
- Reduce clinician time-to-answer (median target: 4–5s). P99 target: <= 10s for triage-critical flows.
- Data residency: pilot is fine on a dedicated VNet in Azure (we will escalate to on-prem if pilot shows PHI exfil concerns).
- Concurrency: estimate 120–150 concurrent during peak; we’ll validate with ops and send telemetry snapshot by EOD Friday.

A couple of asks before we lock the pilot:
1) Can you share SOC2 + encryption-at-rest/key management docs? (see attached questionnaire; we filled parts for Synapse infra and included questions where we need Redwood input).
2) SSO contacts: I’ll introduce our Identity Engineer, Aidan Park, in a follow-up thread.
3) POC timeline: target 6–8 week pilot (2 weeks integration + 4–6 weeks evaluation).

Attached: synapse_security_q1_filled.xlsx (we highlighted several items we need you to confirm).

We can do Thu 7/30 10:00 PT for the tech deep-dive. Please send calendar invite.

Thanks —
Kira
